title: The Price of Love
content:
Siddu lowered his head for a moment before continuing.

"The next few seconds..."

"...changed everything."

His voice grew quieter.

"The principal entered the classroom."

Sneha's eyes widened.

"He saw both of us standing together."

"I didn't even get a chance to explain."

"He rushed toward us, grabbed my arm, and pulled me away from Shreya."

Siddu instinctively touched his cheek, as though he could still feel the pain.

"Before I could utter a single word, his hand struck my cheek with a sharp crack that echoed through the classroom."

"The entire classroom fell silent."

"I wasn't hurt because of the slap."

"I was hurt because I could only watch Shreya standing there..."

"...frightened and helpless."

His eyes slowly lowered.

"The principal dragged me straight to his cabin, leaving Shreya behind."

"Once we reached his office, he didn't ask me for an explanation."

"He simply picked up the phone and called my father."

"I stood there silently as he told my father everything that had happened."

Then, looking straight into my eyes, he said,

"You're suspended from college for one month."

A bitter smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"One month..."

He let out a slow breath.

"And my JEE Main examination was only a few months away."

"The principal pointed toward the door."

"Now get out of my campus."

"It all happened within a matter of minutes."

Sneha stared at Siddu in disbelief.

"What?"

"Is that true?"

"How could he suspend a student for an entire month just before the JEE examination?"

Siddu quietly nodded.

Before he could answer, Yashwanth spoke.

"It happened."

The room fell silent again.

Sneha looked back at Siddu.

"Then... what did you do?"

Siddu took a deep breath.

"I slowly walked back toward my classroom."

"My mind was completely blank."

"Only a few questions kept repeating inside my head."

How am I going to face my father?

How will I spend an entire month without even seeing Shreya?

What will happen to my studies?

"I didn't have an answer to any of them."

"When I entered the classroom..."

"...everyone had already left."

"There was only one person waiting for me."

"Shreya."

"The moment she saw me, she hurried toward me."

"What happened?"

"What did the principal say?"

"I forced myself to smile."

"He informed my parents..."

"...and suspended me for one month."

"After saying those words, I quietly walked toward my desk and began collecting my books."

"Before I could finish..."

"Shreya suddenly came closer."

"Without saying a single word..."

"She wrapped her arms tightly around me."

"I could feel her shoulders trembling."

"Warm tears soaked my shirt."

"For a few moments, time itself seemed to stop."

"Neither of us cared about the empty classroom, the footsteps echoing outside, or the fear of being seen again."

"All the pain we had silently carried for months found its way into that single embrace."

"I could feel her trembling."

"She wasn't just crying..."

"It felt as though every emotion she had buried for months was finally pouring out."

"Her tears carried every unspoken word, every unanswered question, and every helpless moment we had endured since the day we were forced apart."

"I tried..." she whispered through her tears.

"I wanted to explain everything... but nothing went the way I hoped."

"Those few words shattered the last bit of strength I had been holding onto."

"I wanted to ask her countless questions."

"Why had she disappeared?"

"What had really happened during those three months?"

"Why had she never contacted me?"

"But looking at her fragile state, none of those questions mattered anymore."

"All I wanted was for her to stop crying."

"I'm sorry..."

"She whispered repeatedly."

"For a moment..."

"Every part of me wanted to hug her back."

"To tell her everything would be alright."

"But another thought stopped me."

"If the principal saw us again..."

"He might punish her too."

"Slowly..."

"I kept my hands by my side."

"I didn't return her embrace."

"Shreya understood why."

"After a few painful moments, she gently stepped back."

"She wiped the tears from her face and looked at me one last time."

"Neither of us spoke."

"There were no promises."

"No goodbye."

"Only silence..."

"Tears..."

"And two hearts that wanted to stay together but had no choice but to part."

"Taking a deep breath, I picked up my bag..."

"...and slowly walked out of the classroom."

"As I stepped out of the classroom, I resisted the urge to look back."

"Somewhere behind me, I knew Shreya was still standing there."

"But I didn't turn around."

"Deep inside, I knew that if I saw her one more time..."

"I would never find the strength to walk away."

"So I kept moving forward."

"Each step felt heavier than the last."

"The corridor I had walked through every day no longer felt familiar."

"For the first time..."

"It no longer felt like my college."

"It felt like the place where I had lost everything that mattered to me."

"Little did I know..."

"That day wasn't the end of my suffering."

"It was only the beginning."

"Life still had far crueler surprises waiting for me."
